newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-DU PLESSIS HITS BACK AT ALL BLACK CRITICISM.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DU PLESSIS HITS BACK AT ALL BLACK CRITICISM.

text.p: Springbok rugby coach Carel du Plessis has hit back at comments by All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick and coach John Hart in the wake of New Zealand's record 55-35 victory over South Africa.
"I believe they could not compete with us physically so they resorted to a slanging match," du Plessis told reporters when the team arrived in Johannesburg on Tuesday.
"It is absolute nonsense to say that we targeted them in the rucks. They could not compete with us."

South Africa had flanker Andre Venter sent off for stamping on Fitzgerald and winger James Small yellow-carded during the Eden Park match which saw them concede more points than any previous Springbok side.
After the match Hart said he was surprised at the manner in which du Plessis had defended the Springboks' discipline.
Fitzpatrick was disappointed at the way Josh Kronfeld was "unecessarily and blatantly worked over by Mark Andrews".

Du Plessis said: "Their comments are typical New Zealand stuff, but they are hiding the facts. They again committed a number of professional fouls, such as wilfully falling over the player or ball to prevent a tackled player from releasing the ball."
It was South Africa's third successive defeat in the Tri-Nations series and the fifth in seven matches since du Plessis took over as coach .
He claimed he was not affected by the mounting pressure in South Africa for his early removal from a job he took over only six months ago.
"After the (All Black) test SARFU president Louis Luyt said he would back me. I have a three-year contract, although it will be discussed at the end of the season," said du Plessis.
